primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Adult granulosa cell tumor of the ovary
mechanism: Granulosa cell tumors retain normal granulosa-cell steroidogenic functions. FSH signaling induces aromatase (CYP19A1) in granulosa cells, allowing conversion of theca-derived androgens to estrogens. Estrogen excess from a granulosa cell tumor can stimulate the endometrium and cause abnormal uterine bleeding or endometrial hyperplasia.
vignette: A 58-year-old woman who completed menopause 6 years ago presents with new uterine bleeding. Pelvic ultrasonography shows a unilateral ovarian mass and a thickened endometrium. Endometrial biopsy shows simple hyperplasia without atypia. The ovarian mass is resected; histology shows small uniform cells with grooved nuclei surrounding eosinophilic fluid-filled spaces consistent with Call-Exner bodies. Tumor cells stain for inhibin.
lead: Which normal physiologic function of the tumor’s cell of origin most directly explains this patient’s endometrial abnormality?
correct: FSH-stimulated aromatization of theca-derived androgens to estrogens
distractors: LH-stimulated conversion of cholesterol to androgens in theca interna cells
5-alpha-reduction of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone in androgen-responsive tissues
21-hydroxylation of progesterone intermediates in the adrenal zona fasciculata
Desmolase-mediated conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone in Leydig cells
distractor_notes: Theca interna cells respond primarily to LH and generate androgen substrate, but the tumor derives from granulosa cells and the endometrial effect results from granulosa-cell estrogen production.
5-alpha-reductase generates dihydrotestosterone in androgen-responsive tissues and does not explain estrogen excess from an ovarian granulosa cell tumor.
21-hydroxylase is an adrenal steroidogenic enzyme and is unrelated to the ovarian estrogen-producing phenotype shown here.
Leydig cells can convert cholesterol to steroid precursors under LH stimulation, but they are not the cell of origin of this ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor.
key_expl: The ovarian tumor is an adult granulosa cell tumor, identified by Call-Exner bodies, nuclear grooves, and inhibin positivity. Granulosa cells normally express FSH receptors. FSH increases aromatase activity, enabling granulosa cells to convert androstenedione produced by LH-stimulated theca cells into estrogens. Granulosa cell tumors can preserve this steroidogenic phenotype and produce excess estrogen, which stimulates endometrial proliferation and can cause postmenopausal bleeding and endometrial hyperplasia.
objective: Link the hyperestrogenic presentation of a granulosa cell tumor to normal granulosa-cell physiology: FSH-induced aromatization of theca-derived androgen substrate.

sources.locator: Introduction; Pathophysiology; History and Physical; Evaluation
sources.support: NCBI describes granulosa cell tumors as ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors that often retain hormone production, frequently produce estrogen, can cause postmenopausal or abnormal uterine bleeding and endometrial effects, and characteristically show inhibin positivity and adult-type histologic features including nuclear grooves and Call-Exner bodies.
